sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: It's a Friday evening at an apartment in Lower Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 这是曼哈顿下城一间公寓里的周五傍晚。

sentences.en: Two friends are looking forward to unwinding after a long week.
sentences.zh: 两个朋友正期待着在漫长的一周后放松一下。

sentences.en: Their names are Ansel Scholl and Matthias Corona.
sentences.zh: 他们叫安塞尔·绍尔和马蒂亚斯·科罗纳。

sentences.en: And they can teach us all something about friendship.
sentences.zh: 他们能教给我们所有人关于友谊的道理。

sentences.en: They've been friends for half their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们做朋友已经有他们人生一半的时间了。

sentences.en: Like seven years.
sentences.zh: 比如七年。

sentences.en: No, because if it's second grade, third grade, fourth grade, fifth grade, sixth grade, seventh grade, six years.
sentences.zh: 不对，因为如果是二年级、三年级、四年级、五年级、六年级、七年级，那就是六年。

sentences.en: Oh, six years, sorry.
sentences.zh: 哦，六年，抱歉。

sentences.en: Doing the math, that means they're now 12.
sentences.zh: 算一下，这意味着他们现在12岁。

sentences.en: And like ever since second grade, we've been close friends.
sentences.zh: 而且就像从二年级开始，我们就一直是好朋友。

sentences.en: By fourth grade.
sentences.zh: 到四年级的时候。

sentences.en: I mean, I knew that this was going to be my best friend.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道这将成为我最好的朋友。

sentences.en: Their best friendship has involved doing lots of homework together, video games.
sentences.zh: 他们最深厚的友谊包括一起做很多家庭作业、玩电子游戏。

sentences.en: We FaceTime.
sentences.zh: 我们打FaceTime视频。

sentences.en: We help each other.
sentences.zh: 我们互相帮助。

sentences.en: He helps me.
sentences.zh: 他帮助我。

sentences.zh: 我帮助他。

sentences.en: We give each other advice.
sentences.zh: 我们互相给对方出谋划策。

sentences.en: Sleepovers, like the one they're going to have tonight.
sentences.zh: 还有过夜派对，就像他们今晚要办的那样。

sentences.en: Come on, come on, come on.
sentences.zh: 来吧，来吧，来吧。

sentences.en: And Legos.

sentences.en: No, you have to push it.
sentences.zh: 不对，你得按下去。

sentences.zh: 我觉得你得使劲按。

sentences.en: It's not going to go on.
sentences.zh: 它按不上去。

sentences.en: When they're not doing homework or playing together, the two friends are supporting each other.
sentences.zh: 当他们不写作业或一起玩耍时，这两个朋友一直在互相支持。

sentences.en: So my great-grandfather died like a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 所以我的曾祖父几周前去世了。

sentences.en: He really helped me like sort of like get through that.
sentences.zh: 他真的帮我度过了那个难关。

sentences.en: I came up, I'm like, I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 我走过去，我说，我太难过了。

sentences.en: And I hugged him.
sentences.zh: 然后我拥抱了他。

sentences.en: And I don't know if I did it again.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否又这么做了。

sentences.en: But I do remember, I do recall saying it sometimes.
sentences.zh: 但我确实记得，我确实回想起来有时说过这话。

sentences.en: Not trying to be braggy or show him like, oh, I'm so amazing.
sentences.zh: 不是想吹牛或者向他显摆，哦，我太棒了。

sentences.en: But yes, I remember being there for him.
sentences.zh: 但是的，我记得我曾陪伴在他身边。

sentences.en: Ansel and Matthias don't think their friendship will change when they get to high school.
sentences.zh: 安塞尔和马蒂亚斯认为他们上了高中后友谊也不会改变。

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure we'll stay best friends.
sentences.zh: 我很确定我们会一直是好朋友。

sentences.en: That's, yeah, as long as like neither of us move high schools, I think we will.
sentences.zh: 那就是，是的，只要我们两个都不转学去不同的高中，我想我们会一直是的。

sentences.en: And why would they think differently?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么会产生不同的想法呢？

sentences.en: They have the kind of friendship that most kids, or adults for that matter, would want.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有大多数孩子，甚至成年人所渴望的那种友谊。

sentences.en: But for many young men just a few years older than Ansel and Matthias, friendships like this are a distant memory.
sentences.zh: 但是对于许多比安塞尔和马蒂亚斯大几岁的年轻男性来说，这样的友谊已成遥远的记忆。

sentences.en: Some of the boys go into sort of, I don't care, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 有些男孩会表现得好像，我不在乎，这无所谓。

sentences.en: But they say, I don't care so many times that you sense exactly that they do very much care.
sentences.zh: 但他们说“我不在乎”说了太多次，以至于你完全能感觉到他们其实非常在乎。

sentences.en: By the time boys become men, they may not have any friends around, close or otherwise.
sentences.zh: 等男孩们长成男人时，他们身边可能没有任何朋友，无论是挚友还是普通朋友。

sentences.en: It was just this sense of isolation.
sentences.zh: 只有这种孤立感。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, it was just me.
sentences.zh: 到头来，只有我一个人。

sentences.en: Anyway, many men find there's no one around them at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 总之，许多男人发现到头来身边空无一人。

sentences.en: And they find they have become trapped by a series of unspoken rules.
sentences.zh: 并且他们发现自己被一系列心照不宣的规则所束缚。

sentences.en: If you're a man, you're supposed to be strong and independent.
sentences.zh: 如果你是个男人，你就应该坚强而独立。

sentences.en: If you connect deeply, especially with other men, it's probably because you're gay.
sentences.zh: 如果你建立深度的联系，尤其是与其他男性，那很可能是因为你是同性恋。

sentences.en: If you crave deep emotional bonds, well, that's just unmanly.
sentences.zh: 如果你渴望深的情感纽带，好吧，那太没有男子气概了。

sentences.en: Today on Hidden Brain, we take a closer look at misguided notions of masculinity in the United States.
sentences.zh: 今天在《隐藏的大脑》中，我们仔细审视美国对男子气概的错误观念。

sentences.en: And we explore new research that studies the consequences.
sentences.zh: 我们探讨研究其后果的新科学。

sentences.en: Stressed out romantic relationships, physical health problems, and a growing epidemic of loneliness.
sentences.zh: 压力重重的浪漫关系、身体健康问题，以及日益蔓延的孤独流行病。

sentences.en: To understand what's going on today, we need to step back 80 years and tell a story that's been passed down and even mythologized.
sentences.zh: 为了理解今天发生了什么，我们需要回溯80年，讲一个代代相传甚至被神话化的故事。

sentences.en: In the late 1930s, a retail store magnate named W.T.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪30年代末，一位零售业巨头名叫W·T·

sentences.en: Grant had a question.
sentences.zh: 格兰特，他有一个问题。

sentences.en: Can you predict who's going to become a good department store manager?
sentences.zh: 你能预测谁会成为一名优秀的百货公司经理吗？

sentences.en: To find out, he teamed up with a Harvard professor named Arlie Bach and gave him $60,000 to run a study.
sentences.zh: 为了找出答案，他与哈佛教授阿利·巴克合作，给了他6万美元开展一项研究。

sentences.en: Dr. Arlie Bach thought that medical research focused too much on what made people sick.
sentences.zh: 阿利·巴克博士认为医学研究过分关注是什么让人生病。

sentences.en: He wanted to know what made people healthy.
sentences.zh: 他想知道是什么让人保持健康。

sentences.en: To answer that question, and presumably W.T.
sentences.zh: 为了回答这个问题，大概还有W·T·

sentences.en: Grant's question about department store managers,
sentences.zh: 格兰特关于百货公司经理的问题，

sentences.en: he and his colleagues picked a group of Harvard students to track closely over time.
sentences.zh: 他和同事们挑选了一群哈佛学生进行长期的密切跟踪。

sentences.en: They chose 268 students, mostly from the classes of 1942, 43, and 44.
sentences.zh: 他们选择了268名学生，主要来自1942、43和44届。

sentences.en: The researchers thought the study would run a decade or so.
sentences.zh: 研究人员以为这项研究会持续十年左右。

sentences.en: All the volunteers were men.
sentences.zh: 所有的志愿者都是男性。

sentences.en: Harvard didn't admit women at the time.
sentences.zh: 哈佛大学当时不招收女性。

sentences.en: All were white.
sentences.zh: 所有人都是白人。

sentences.en: Some students went on to have distinguished careers beyond department store management.
sentences.zh: 一些学生在百货公司管理之外的领域取得了卓越的职业生涯。

sentences.en: One became a swashbuckling newspaper editor.
sentences.zh: 其中一人成为了一位意气风发的报纸编辑。

sentences.en: Ben Bradley not only helped The Washington Post break news, he was the news.
sentences.zh: 本·布拉德利不仅帮助《华盛顿邮报》独家爆料，他自己就是新闻本身。

sentences.en: Any story about The Post must begin with Benjamin Crown and Shield Bradley, 52,
sentences.zh: 任何关于《邮报》的故事都必须从本杰明·克朗希尔德·布拉德利开始，现年52岁，
zh_words: 杰明·克朗希尔德·布拉德利

sentences.en: its fast-talking, chain-smoking, cocky executive editor.
sentences.zh: 他是那个语速极快、烟不离手、趾高气扬的执行总编辑。

sentences.en: Another became president.
sentences.zh: 另一个人成为了总统。

sentences.en: We choose to go to the moon in this decade and do the other thing,
sentences.zh: 我们选择在这十年内登月并完成其他壮举，

sentences.en: not because they are easy, but because they are hard.
sentences.zh: 不是因为它们容易，而是因为它们困难。

sentences.en: Others had hard lives and struggled with mental illness or alcoholism.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则生活艰难，与精神疾病或酗酒作斗争。

sentences.en: As part of the study, these men were put through all kinds of tests.
sentences.zh: 作为研究的一部分，这些男性接受了各种各样的测试。

sentences.en: Researchers measured everything from the size of their moles
sentences.zh: 研究人员测量了从他们的痣的大小

sentences.en: to the lactic acid their bodies released after five minutes on a treadmill.
sentences.zh: 到他们在跑步机上跑五分钟后身体释放的乳酸的一切指标。

sentences.en: The men were asked to interpret Rorschach inkblots.
sentences.zh: 受试者被要求解读罗夏墨迹图。

sentences.en: Their handwriting was analyzed.
sentences.zh: 他们的笔迹得到了分析。

sentences.en: Examiners took detailed measurements of their skulls.
sentences.zh: 检查人员对他们的头骨进行了详细测量。

sentences.en: At the time, researchers thought the size and shape of a head
sentences.zh: 当时，研究人员认为头部的大小和形状

sentences.en: could tell you a great deal about a person's character and abilities.
sentences.zh: 可以透露出一个人的大量性格和能力信息。

sentences.en: So we now have a whole set of elaborate skull measurements
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在拥有一整套精心制作的头骨测量数据，

sentences.en: that we have no idea what to do with.
sentences.zh: 而我们完全不知道该拿它们怎么办。

sentences.en: This is Robert Waldinger.
sentences.zh: 这是罗伯特·瓦尔丁格。

sentences.en: He is the current director of the project.
sentences.zh: 他是该项目现任负责人。

sentences.en: It's now called the Harvard Study of Adult Development.
sentences.zh: 它现在被称为哈佛成人发展研究。

sentences.en: It's lasted far longer than Arleigh Bach and W.T.
sentences.zh: 它的持续时间远超阿利·巴克和W·T·

sentences.en: Grant imagined.
sentences.zh: 格兰特的想象。

sentences.en: It's now been running for eight decades.
sentences.zh: 它现在已经进行了八个十年。

sentences.en: The length of the study isn't the only thing that's unusual.
sentences.zh: 这项研究的持续时间并不是唯一不寻常的地方。

sentences.en: Its aims were hazy.
sentences.zh: 它的目标很模糊。

sentences.en: Sure, it was supposed to look broadly at who does well.
sentences.zh: 当然，它本意是广泛观察谁能成功。

sentences.en: But research studies are often designed to test one or two specific questions.
sentences.zh: 但研究通常旨在测试一个或两个具体问题。

sentences.en: The aims of this study were nebulous,
sentences.zh: 这项研究的目标是含糊不清的，

sentences.en: and they changed repeatedly over the years.
sentences.zh: 而且多年来一再改变。

sentences.en: Sometimes we've been called the biggest fishing expedition
sentences.zh: 有时我们被称为历史上最大的

sentences.en: in the history of research.
sentences.zh: 漫无目的的研究搜寻行动。

sentences.en: As the years went by, the study's agenda changed
sentences.zh: 随着岁月流逝，随着新资助者的涌入和科学的发展，

sentences.en: as new funders swept in and science evolved.
sentences.zh: 研究的议程也随之改变。

sentences.zh: 身心之间的联系

sentences.en: became more of a concern in the 1980s and 90s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪80和90年代变得更加受关注。

sentences.en: One thing the study paid attention to from the very start
sentences.zh: 这项研究从一开始就关注的一件事

sentences.en: was the volunteer's social and emotional lives.
sentences.zh: 就是志愿者的社交和情感生活。

sentences.en: Arleigh Bach was prescient in that way.
sentences.zh: 阿利·巴克在这方面很有先见之明。

sentences.en: He had a psychiatrist on his team,
sentences.zh: 他的团队里有一位精神病学家，

sentences.en: and there were extensive interviews
sentences.zh: 并且进行了广泛的访谈，

sentences.en: about the young men's emotional lives.
sentences.zh: 内容关于这些年轻男性的情感生活。

sentences.zh: 还有一些个性评估

sentences.en: and some assessments of their emotional reactivity.
sentences.zh: 以及对他们情绪反应的评估。

sentences.en: So, all the way along,
sentences.zh: 所以，一路走来，

sentences.en: emotional well-being and personality characteristics
sentences.zh: 情感健康和个性特征

sentences.en: were a subject of intereSt.
sentences.zh: 一直是人们感兴趣的主题。

sentences.zh: 从研究的最早日子起，

sentences.zh: 所有男性都被问到一个看似简单的问题。

sentences.en: Who would you call in the middle of the night
sentences.zh: 如果你生病或害怕，

sentences.zh: 你在半夜会打电话给谁？

sentences.zh: 对自己的生活和婚姻更满意。

sentences.zh: 这些男性的回答

sentences.zh: 与他们对该问题的回答之间

sentences.zh: 也存在着联系，与他们的身体健康之间。

sentences.en: that began to emerge in our data in the 80s.

sentences.zh: 我们可能会想到吃得对和进行锻炼。

sentences.zh: 我们不会去问自己是否为友谊留出了足够的时间。

sentences.zh: 而亲密的关系则能保护我们

sentences.zh: 研究人员发现，退休后最幸福的人

sentences.zh: 是那些积极努力用朋友取代同事的人。

sentences.zh: 今天，这项研究将聚焦于这个问题。

sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代，这项研究变得更具代表性

sentences.en: when the study of Harvard men was paired with a separate study happening in Boston.
sentences.zh: 当时哈佛男性的研究与波士顿正在进行的另一项研究结合在了一起。

sentences.en: That research focused on boys from some of the poorest, toughest areas of the city.
sentences.zh: 那项研究聚焦于该市最贫困、最艰难地区的一些男孩。

sentences.en: Together, these studies provide a vivid picture of men's health
sentences.zh: 这些研究合在一起，生动地展现了男性在人生的整个过程中

sentences.en: over the course of their lives.
sentences.zh: 的健康状况。

sentences.en: Now, you could say this research is obviously incomplete
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会说这项研究显然是不完整的

sentences.en: because it leaves out more than half the population.
sentences.zh: 因为它漏掉了半数以上的人口。

sentences.en: But it does tell a striking story about a phenomenon that has many researchers worried.
sentences.zh: 但它的确讲述了一个引人注目的故事，关乎一个让许多研究人员担忧的现象。

sentences.en: Social isolation among men.
sentences.zh: 男性的社会孤立。

sentences.en: I really don't think I dealt with it.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得我没有去面对它。

sentences.en: I think I viewed it as sort of a circumstance rather than a problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为我把它看作是一种环境，而不是一个问题。

sentences.en: But there was also a part of me that realized I was alone.
sentences.zh: 但我的内心深处也意识到自己是孤单的。

sentences.en: When we come back, we look at the profound loneliness of American men.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探讨美国男性的深刻孤独感。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐形大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In recent decades, there have been pervasive worries
sentences.zh: 近几十年来，人们普遍担心

sentences.en: that Americans are spending less time with one another
sentences.zh: 美国人花在彼此陪伴上的时间越来越少

sentences.en: and that the ties that once bound communities together have started to fray.
sentences.zh: 曾经将社区凝聚在一起的纽带已经开始瓦解。

sentences.en: Back in 2000, the political scientist Robert Putnam wrote about this idea in his book,
sentences.zh: 早在2000年，政治学家罗伯特·帕特南在他的书里探讨过这个观点，

sentences.en: Bowling Alone.
sentences.zh: 《独自保龄》。

sentences.en: He described how many Americans were opting out of the civic and community organizations
sentences.zh: 他描述了许多美国人如何选择不再加入

sentences.en: that their parents once joined.
sentences.zh: 他们父母曾经加入的公民和社区组织。

sentences.en: More recently, researchers have watched with growing concern
sentences.zh: 最近，研究人员怀着日益担忧的心情注意到

sentences.en: as many of us spend increasing amounts of time hunched over our phones
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人花越来越多的时间低头看手机

sentences.en: while ignoring those sitting across from us.
sentences.zh: 却忽视了坐在对面的人。

sentences.en: There's another form of social isolation that's less talked about,
sentences.zh: 还有另一种较少被谈论的社会孤立形式，

sentences.en: one that disproportionately affects men.
sentences.zh: 一种对男性影响不成比例的现象。

sentences.en: Men like Paul Kugelman.
sentences.zh: 像保罗·库格尔曼这样的男性。

sentences.en: When Paul was a kid growing up in Union City, New Jersey,
sentences.zh: 保罗小时候在新泽西州联合市长大时，

sentences.en: his parents had a simple rule.
sentences.zh: 他的父母有一个简单的规矩。

sentences.en: Go outside and play and come home when the streetlights come on.
sentences.zh: 出去玩，路灯亮了就回家。

sentences.en: Each weekday, Paul walked to and from school with other kids in his neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 每个工作日，保罗都和邻里的小伙伴一起结伴上下学。

sentences.en: Dawn and George and Joanne and Henry, John.
sentences.zh: 唐、乔治、琼、亨利、约翰。

sentences.en: When the kids got home, they dropped off their books and ran outside to play.
sentences.zh: 孩子们回到家，放下书本就跑出去玩。

sentences.en: We'd do whatever.
sentences.zh: 我们什么都玩。

sentences.en: It was a tag, ring of levio, capture the flag, football, whatever.
sentences.zh: 抓人、抓特务、夺旗、橄榄球，什么都玩。

sentences.en: It was just, it was friendship.
sentences.zh: 那纯粹是，那是友谊。

sentences.en: You had people you could talk to.
sentences.zh: 你有可以倾诉的人。

sentences.en: You were part of a community of your peers.
sentences.zh: 你是同龄人社区的一部分。

sentences.en: It was nice.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉很好。

sentences.en: It was all so easy.
sentences.zh: 一切都那么简单。

sentences.en: Paul played pickup football in the vacant lot across the street from his home.
sentences.zh: 保罗在他家街对面的空地上打自发组织的橄榄球。

sentences.en: He ran into his Aunt Marie at the library.
sentences.zh: 他在图书馆偶遇了玛丽阿姨。

sentences.en: You'd just run into people all the time when you kind of knew everybody in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 只要你对街坊邻居比较熟，你总是会随时随地遇到人。

sentences.en: Then, when Paul was nine, he and his family moved 500 miles south to Martinsville, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 后来，保罗九岁时，他和家人向南搬了500英里，来到了弗吉尼亚州马丁斯维尔。

sentences.en: Rural Virginia didn't have all the amenities he was used to in New Jersey,
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚的农村没有他在新泽西习惯的那些便利设施，

sentences.en: like the black and white cookies and coffee cake he used to get at an iconic bakery.
sentences.zh: 比如他以前常去的那家标志性面包店买的黑白饼干和咖啡蛋糕。

sentences.en: Not only was there no such thing as Entenmann's, it was like, what do you mean by bagel?
sentences.zh: 不仅没有恩特曼糕点这种东西，甚至当别人说百吉饼时，他会想：你说的这是什么？

sentences.en: Paul missed his comfort foods, but that wasn't the only thing that gave him culture shock.
sentences.zh: 保罗怀念他那些慰藉心灵的食物，但这并不是唯一让他感到文化冲击的事情。

sentences.en: It was my first few days in school, and the teacher had a thick southern accent, and she was giving a spelling teSt.
sentences.zh: 那是我在学校的前几天，老师有着浓重的南方口音，她在进行拼写测试。

sentences.en: What I heard was Alpo, but she said apple.
sentences.zh: 我听到的是Alpo（狗粮品牌），但她说的是apple（苹果）。

sentences.en: But I heard Alpo, so I wrote Alpo, and these people concluded that I was a screaming idiot because I didn't understand how to spell apple,
sentences.zh: 但我听到的是Alpo，所以我写下了Alpo，这些人断定我是一个尖叫的傻子，因为我不知道怎么拼写apple，

sentences.en: and I was supposed to be this great student, and it kind of went downhill from there for a while.
sentences.zh: 而我本该是个好学生，从那以后情况有一段时间就有点走下坡路了。

sentences.en: Paul's father was frequently relocated for work, after Virginia to Delaware, then South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 保罗的父亲经常因为工作而搬家，离开弗吉尼亚后去了特拉华州，然后是南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: Each time the family moved, Paul had to navigate a new school and a new social world.
sentences.zh: 每次搬家，保罗都不得不适应一所新学校和一个新的社交世界。

sentences.en: Even though he didn't realize it at the time, he was gradually developing a strategy to cope with all the moves.
sentences.zh: 尽管当时他没有意识到，但他逐渐在培养一种策略来应对所有的搬迁。

sentences.en: I didn't really interact a whole lot with folks, because it just was like, we're going to move again, so I didn't want the pain, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我其实没有跟大伙儿有很多互动，因为感觉就是，我们又要搬家了，所以我不想经历那种痛苦吧。

sentences.en: Paul eventually went off to study at the Citadel, a military college in South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 保罗最终去南卡罗来纳州的军事院校——城堡军校求学。

sentences.en: When he arrived, he was told that his classmates would become lifelong friends.
sentences.zh: 他刚到的时候，有人告诉他，他的同窗将会成为终身的朋友。

sentences.en: But after they graduated, Paul found his former classmates were not very eager to stay in touch.
sentences.zh: 但毕业后，保罗发现他的前同窗们并不是很热衷于保持联系。

sentences.en: Paul's life took its own trajectory.
sentences.zh: 保罗的人生走上了他自己的轨迹。

sentences.en: He got married, had a child, he got divorced.
sentences.zh: 他结婚了，有了孩子，后来又离婚了。

sentences.en: In his 30s, Paul went to law school and remarried.
sentences.zh: 在他30多岁时，保罗去读了法学院并再次结婚。

sentences.en: Just like before, he made acquaintances, but...
sentences.zh: 就像以前一样，他结识了一些泛泛之交，但是……

sentences.en: I was in this place where, in my mind, everything was kind of transient.
sentences.zh: 我当时处在这样一个地方，在我的脑海里，一切都是短暂的。

sentences.en: He didn't quite realize it, but his social world was shrinking.
sentences.zh: 他并没有完全意识到，但他的社交世界正在缩小。

sentences.en: The acquaintances he made stayed acquaintances.
sentences.zh: 他结识的泛泛之交依然只是泛泛之交。

sentences.en: He didn't have the time to develop these into real friendships.
sentences.zh: 他没有时间将这些关系发展成真正的友谊。

sentences.en: Family and work felt all-consuming.
sentences.zh: 家庭和工作让人感觉占据了全部精力。

sentences.en: In his mid-40s, Paul's second marriage fell apart.
sentences.zh: 在他40岁出头时，保罗的第二段婚姻破裂了。

sentences.en: His ex-wife took the kids and moved several hours away.
sentences.zh: 他的前妻带着孩子搬到了几个小时车程之外的地方。

sentences.en: His mother had died young, and Paul was estranged from his father.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲很早就去世了，保罗与父亲也疏远了。

sentences.en: He talked to his daughter every day, but that routine ended too.
sentences.zh: 他每天都跟女儿通话，但那个常规也结束了。

sentences.en: Even though he was doing meaningful work as a lawyer, it wasn't enough.
sentences.zh: 尽管他作为一名律师做着有意义的工作，但这还不够。

sentences.en: I guess lonely is the right word.
sentences.zh: 我想“孤独”是正确的词。

sentences.en: It was a very lonely time.
sentences.zh: 那是一段非常孤独的时期。

sentences.en: I don't remember specific triggers.
sentences.zh: 我不记得有什么具体的导火索。

sentences.en: It was just this sense of absolute isolation.
sentences.zh: 只有那种绝对孤立的感觉。

sentences.en: Absolute's too strong a word.
sentences.zh: “绝对”这个词用得太重了。

sentences.en: Because I did go to work, and I did have interactions at work.
sentences.zh: 因为我的确去上班了，而且我在工作中的确有互动。

sentences.en: And I cherished those.
sentences.zh: 我很珍惜那些互动。

sentences.en: But, you know, at the end of the day, it was just me.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，到头来，只有我一个人。

sentences.en: He drank heavily for a while.
sentences.zh: 他有一段时间酗酒得很厉害。

sentences.en: Then, he got into exercise.
sentences.zh: 后来，他迷上了运动。

sentences.en: He eventually completed an Ironman triathlon.
sentences.zh: 他最终完成了铁人三项比赛。

sentences.en: But these distractions couldn't quite stamp out the fact that he was desperate for friendship,
sentences.zh: 但这些分心的事情无法抹杀这样一个事实：他极度渴望友谊，

sentences.en: for connection, so desperate that he turned to an inanimate object for comfort.
sentences.zh: 渴望连接，以至于他转向一个无生命的物体寻求安慰。

sentences.en: I was in my apartment, and one of the fixtures in the apartment was a post that runs floor to ceiling,
sentences.zh: 当时我在公寓里，公寓里的固定设施之一是一根从地板通到天花板的柱子，

sentences.en: and a banister runs out of that.
sentences.zh: 有一根扶手从那根柱子延伸出来。

sentences.en: And the post became my friend.
sentences.zh: 那根柱子成了我的朋友。

sentences.en: I would hug the poSt.
sentences.zh: 我会拥抱那根柱子。

sentences.en: I would hug the post for all it was worth, because I was getting some kind of feedback physically.
sentences.zh: 我会尽全力拥抱那根柱子，因为我从身体上得到了一些反馈。

sentences.en: It was at that point I realized, I have got to do something,
sentences.zh: 就在那时我意识到，我必须做点什么，

sentences.en: because when you get to the place where you need to hug a post to feel something that you need,
sentences.zh: 因为当你落到需要拥抱一根柱子来获得你所需的某种感觉时，

sentences.en: if that's not a wake-up call, nothing is.
sentences.zh: 如果这还算不上警钟，那就没有什么是了。

sentences.en: Paul's childhood offered a model of a close-knit community.
sentences.zh: 保罗的童年提供了一个紧密团结的社区的模范。

sentences.en: His life in his 40s was nothing like that model.
sentences.zh: 他40多岁时的生活与那个模范完全不沾边。

sentences.en: Looking back, Paul says he ignored the warning signs that his social world was shrinking.
sentences.zh: 回首过去，保罗说他忽视了社交世界正在缩小的警告信号。

sentences.en: I really don't think I dealt with it, candidly.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我真的觉得我没有去处理它。

sentences.en: I think I viewed it as sort of a circumstance rather than a problem.
sentences.zh: 我想我把它看作是一种环境，而不是一个问题。

sentences.en: It's kind of like gravity.
sentences.zh: 这有点像地心引力。

sentences.en: But there was also a part of me that realized I was alone.
sentences.zh: 但我的内心深处也意识到自己是孤单的。

sentences.en: Even when Paul got the courage to reach out to other people,
sentences.zh: 甚至当保罗鼓起勇气向其他人伸出援手时，

sentences.en: he found himself butting up against social rules.
sentences.zh: 他发现自己处处碰壁，违背了社交规则。

sentences.en: He went to introduce himself to neighbors in his apartment building,
sentences.zh: 他去公寓楼里向邻居做自我介绍，

sentences.en: but found them more bewildered than friendly.
sentences.zh: 却发现对方与其说是友好，不如说是感到困惑。

sentences.en: It's not like anything they said in particular.
sentences.zh: 倒不是他们说的具体内容有什么问题。

sentences.en: It's kind of the look, the countenance.
sentences.zh: 有点像是那个眼神，那种神情。

sentences.en: Like, you're an odd dude.
sentences.zh: 就像是在说，你是个奇怪的家伙。

sentences.en: Why is a 51-year-old guy knocking on our door to tell us he lives next door?
sentences.zh: 一个51岁的男人为什么来敲我们的门，告诉我们他住在隔壁？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Part of it is I think there's a stigma to being viewed as being alone or lonely.
sentences.zh: 部分原因我认为是被视为孤单或孤独带有某种污名化。

sentences.en: The irony was Paul himself wasn't very forgiving to people who were in the same boat that he was.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，保罗自己对那些处境和他一样的人也并不宽容。

sentences.en: It's funny, like when I got out into the dating realm again, you know, I'm this middle-aged alone person,
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，比如当我重新回到约会领域时，你知道的，我是一个中年孤单的人，

sentences.en: but I'm very wary of people who are in the same group as I am because, you know, what are you doing at this age alone?
sentences.zh: 但我对处于和我同一群组的人非常警惕，因为，你知道的，你这么大年纪了怎么还孤身一人？

sentences.en: Over and over, Paul was reminded that it was hard for a middle-aged man to form meaningful new friendships.
sentences.zh: 保罗一次又一次地被提醒，中年男子很难建立起有意义的新友谊。

sentences.en: After he started dating, he noticed how his girlfriend Kim easily struck up conversations and made new connections.
sentences.zh: 开始约会后，他注意到他的女友金是如何轻易地开启对话并建立新联系的。

sentences.en: She can make friends anywhere she goes, and nobody bats an eye about a woman going up and just chatting either a guy or a girl up.
sentences.zh: 无论走到哪里她都能交到朋友，而且无论女人上去跟男人还是女人闲聊，都不会有人觉得奇怪。

sentences.en: It wasn't just Kim.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是金。

sentences.en: It felt like there was a difference between men and women.
sentences.zh: 感觉男人和女人之间确实存在差异。

sentences.en: At one point, they were at a festival.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他们在一个节日活动上。

sentences.en: Seemingly out of nowhere, Kim's friend Polly gathered together seven or eight people to hang out.
sentences.zh: 仿佛凭空出现一般，金的朋友波莉召集了七八个人一起玩。

sentences.en: And I had this feeling if I tried to do that, it would be like, okay, who's the creepy old dude, you know?
sentences.zh: 而我有这样一种感觉：如果我试着那样做，大家会觉得，好吧，这个阴森的中年大叔是谁啊，你知道吗？

sentences.en: But I think there is a stigma for guys, and I don't know if it's just a, you know, a self-imposed thing or actually society views it that way.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对男人来说确实存在一种污名，我不知道这只是一种，你知道的，自寻烦恼还是社会确实是这么看的。

sentences.en: From my experience, I think society views it that way, but I can't say for sure.
sentences.zh: 从我的经验来看，我认为社会就是这么看的，但我无法百分之百确定。

sentences.en: He now recognizes that even though it's hard, reaching out to other people is essential.
sentences.zh: 他现在认识到，尽管很难，但向其他人伸出援手是至关重要的。

sentences.en: A rejection of the extension of an offer of friendship or acquaintancehood isn't a rejection.
sentences.zh: 对建立友谊或泛泛之交的邀请的拒绝并不是对你个人的拒绝。

sentences.en: It's just that that person's not ready.
sentences.zh: 只是那个人还没准备好。

sentences.en: Paul's story is echoed by many other men who reached out to us in recent months.
sentences.zh: 保罗的故事得到了近几个月来与我们联系的许多其他男性的共鸣。

sentences.en: Although each story is different in the details, the same themes run through many of them.
sentences.zh: 尽管每个故事在细节上各不相同，但许多故事都贯穿着相同的主题。

sentences.en: These men felt they didn't have enough friends.
sentences.zh: 这些男性觉得自己的朋友不够多。

sentences.en: Even when they wanted to make new friends, they didn't know how to do it.
sentences.zh: 即使他们想结新朋友，也不知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: I really look back on the last 50, such a durSt.
sentences.zh: 我真的很回味过去的50年，真是一段坎坷的旅程。

sentences.en: I'm married, and when my wife and I are together, there are things to do and not enough time in the day to do them with our friends.
sentences.zh: 我结婚了，我和妻子在一起时，有很多事情要做，而一天的时间根本不够和我们的朋友们一起完成这些事。

sentences.en: When she and I are apart for more than a day or two, I turn into a hermit.
sentences.zh: 当我和她分开超过一天或两天时，我就变成了一个隐士。

sentences.en: Many married men reported that their wives organized their social activities.
sentences.zh: 许多已婚男性表示，他们的社交活动是由妻子安排的。

sentences.en: In a recent episode of Hidden Brain, psychologist Eli Finkel explained how such over-reliance on one person is a new phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 在近期的一期《隐藏的大脑》节目中，心理学家伊利·芬克尔解释了为什么对某一个人产生这种过度依赖是一个新现象。

sentences.en: There was a time not long ago in the United States when people didn't expect their spouse to be partner and lover and best friend combined.
sentences.zh: 不久前在美国，人们并不指望配偶既是伴侣、爱人又是最好的朋友。

sentences.en: Marriage for a long time served a set and relatively limited array of different functions for us.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，婚姻对我们而言发挥着一套相对有限的各种固定功能。

sentences.en: And over time, we've piled more and more of these emotional and psychological functions.
sentences.zh: 而随着时间的推移，我们把越来越多的情感和心理功能压在了婚姻上。

sentences.en: So instead of turning to our close friends and other relatives for nights out on the town, for deep, intimate disclosure,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们不再去找密友和其他亲戚进行夜生活、倾诉内心深处的秘密，

sentences.en: to a larger and larger extent, our spouse has replaced a lot of what we used to look to our broader social network to help us do.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上，我们的配偶取代了许多我们过去习惯于向更广泛的社交网络寻求帮助的事情。

sentences.en: If many men in heterosexual relationships count on wives to be their sole providers of social connection,
sentences.zh: 如果异性恋关系中的许多男性指望妻子成为他们社交联系的唯一提供者，

sentences.en: this places enormous pressure on women in those relationships too.
sentences.zh: 这也给这些关系中的女性带来了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: To be sure, there are exceptions to all of this.
sentences.zh: 当然，所有这些情况都有例外。

sentences.en: But overall, researchers are worried about increasing social isolation among men and where this might lead.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，研究人员对男性的社会孤立感日益加剧以及这可能导致的后果感到担忧。

sentences.en: Some men cope not by running an Ironman or drinking or hugging an inanimate object.
sentences.zh: 有些男性的应对方式不是去参加铁人三项、借酒消愁或拥抱无生命的物体。

sentences.en: They take more drastic measures.
sentences.zh: 他们采取了更极端的措施。

sentences.en: I spoke to Julie Phillips about this.
sentences.zh: 我为此采访了朱莉·菲利普斯。

sentences.en: She's a sociology professor at Rutgers University.
sentences.zh: 她是罗格斯大学的社会学教授。

sentences.en: Which figure are you looking at here?
sentences.zh: 你在这里看的是哪个图表？

sentences.en: I'll see if it is figure two.
sentences.zh: 我看看是不是图二。

sentences.en: She walked me through a couple of graphs that show the rate of suicide among men of different age groups.
sentences.zh: 她带我浏览了几张展示不同年龄段男性自杀率的图表。

sentences.en: Those rates vary widely from the young to the very old.
sentences.zh: 这些比率从年轻人到老年人差异很大。

sentences.en: Increasingly, however, middle-aged men appear to be at growing risk.
sentences.zh: 然而，中年男性面临的风险似乎正日益增加。

sentences.en: We saw a fairly sharp increase in suicide rates among men beginning in 1999.
sentences.zh: 我们发现从1999年开始，男性的自杀率出现了相当急剧的增长。

sentences.en: So, for example, among men aged 50 to 54, we saw an increase of almost 50% in their suicide rate.
sentences.zh: 例如，在50至54岁的男性中，我们看到他们的自杀率增长了近50%。

sentences.en: The increase in the suicide rate among middle-aged men is troubling.
sentences.zh: 中年男性自杀率的上升令人不安。

sentences.en: It's also a reversal of historical patterns.
sentences.zh: 这也是对历史规律的一种逆转。

sentences.en: Compared to earlier generations, the uptick in suicide seems to be starting earlier and earlier, especially for men.
sentences.zh: 与早期几代人相比，自杀率的上升似乎出现得越来越早，尤其是对男性而言。

sentences.en: One common interpretation of this trend is that it's driven by economic probleMs.
sentences.zh: 对这种趋势的一种常见解释是，它是受经济问题驱动的。

sentences.en: Julie thinks it's more complicated.
sentences.zh: 朱莉认为事情要复杂得多。

sentences.en: The trend of rising suicide rates among middle-aged men began in the late 1990s, well before the Great Recession that started in 2007.
sentences.zh: 中年男性自杀率上升的趋势始于20世纪90年代末，远早于2007年开始的大衰退。

sentences.en: Actually, from 1999 to 2005, the increases among the middle-aged were really confined to those boomers who did not have a college education.
sentences.zh: 事实上，从1999年到2005年，中年人自杀率的增长实际上仅限于那些没有受过大学教育的婴儿潮一代。

sentences.en: But since 2005, it has now broadened out.
sentences.zh: 但自2005年以来，这种现象已经扩大了。

sentences.en: It's really been across the board.
sentences.zh: 它确实已经蔓延到了各个阶层。

sentences.en: We don't see these differences by education.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到因教育背景不同而产生的这些差异。

sentences.en: Julie has other ideas about what might be driving these changes.
sentences.zh: 对于是什么在推动这些变化，朱莉有其他的看法。

sentences.en: People have fewer social supports.
sentences.zh: 人们的社会支持变少了。

sentences.en: They're more likely to live far away from family.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能远离家人居住。

sentences.en: Many are opting out of marriage.
sentences.zh: 许多人选择不结婚。

sentences.en: Many are getting divorced.
sentences.zh: 许多人正在离婚。

sentences.en: Even when we choose to connect with others, we're often not doing it in person.
sentences.zh: 即使我们选择与他人联系，往往也不是通过面对面的方式。

sentences.en: I also wonder, too, just about the ways in which we interact and how that has changed certainly over the past 15, 20 years or so.
sentences.zh: 我也在想，我们的互动方式以及过去15年或20年左右这种方式发生了怎样的变化。

sentences.en: So, I mean, the rise of social media, less face-to-face contact, you know, our entertainment has sort of become more private.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，社交媒体的兴起，面对面接触减少，你知道，我们的娱乐变得更加私人化了。

sentences.en: You know, we watch a movie at home rather than going to a theater, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，你知道，我们在家里看电影，而不是去电影院。

sentences.en: So, you know, that may also be having, it may be contributing to feelings of isolation, social isolation that could also be producing some of these rising rates.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这可能也会产生影响，可能会导致孤立感，即社会孤立感，这也可能会导致其中一些不断上升的自杀率。

sentences.en: Again, the toll of social isolation isn't just emotional.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，社会孤立带来的代价不仅仅是情感上的。

sentences.en: An analysis of nearly 150 studies has found that people with strong social relationships had about a 50% lower mortality risk than those with weaker ties.
sentences.zh: 一项对近150项研究的分析发现，拥有牢固社会关系的人的死亡风险比社交关系薄弱的人低约50%。

sentences.en: Julianne Holt-Lunstad and her co-authors concluded that those with weaker social relationships had a greater risk of death than people who were physically inactive or obese.
sentences.zh: 朱莉安·霍尔特-伦斯塔德和她的合著者得出结论，社会关系薄弱的人比缺乏身体活动或肥胖的人面临更大的死亡风险。
zh_words: 朱莉安·霍尔特-伦斯塔德

sentences.en: Let me put that another way.
sentences.zh: 让我换个方式表达。

sentences.en: Spending time building and nurturing your friendships might be just as important to your health as eating right and exercising.
sentences.zh: 花时间建立和培养你的友谊，对你的健康而言可能与吃得健康和锻炼一样重要。

sentences.en: When we come back, we look at the cultural roots of this problem.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将探讨这个问题的文化根源。

sentences.en: These are, you know, human beings with unbelievable emotional and social capacity.
sentences.zh: 这些，你知道的，是具有难以置信的情感和社会能力的人类。

sentences.en: And we as a culture just completely try to zip it out of them.
sentences.zh: 而我们作为一种文化，却极力试图将这些从他们身上抹杀掉。

sentences.en: And we ignore it.
sentences.zh: 我们对此视而不见。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: We're exploring the effects of social isolation over the course of our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们正在探讨社会孤立贯穿我们一生的影响。

sentences.en: In particular, we're looking at men who tend to have a harder time than women when it comes to making and maintaining friendships.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我们在关注那些在结交和维持友谊方面往往比女性更艰难的男性。

sentences.en: Economic forces certainly play a role in eroding social ties.
sentences.zh: 经济力量无疑在侵蚀社会联系方面发挥了作用。

sentences.en: But psychologist Niobe Way thinks that the roots of loneliness among men go deeper.
sentences.zh: 但心理学家尼奥比·韦认为，男性孤独的根源更深。

sentences.en: She thinks they are primarily cultural, embedded, and twisted ideas of what it takes to be a man.
sentences.zh: 她认为它们主要是文化层面的，是关于如何做一个男人的根深蒂固且扭曲的观念。

sentences.en: In the late 1980s, Niobe worked as a counselor at a high school in Boston.
sentences.zh: 20世纪80年代末，尼奥比在波士顿的一所高中担任辅导员。

sentences.en: She expected the boys in her school to talk about their classes, difficulties with family, violence in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 她原本以为她学校里的男孩们会谈论他们的课程、家庭困难以及社区里的暴力事件。

sentences.en: What they were mostly talking about is their friendships and trying to find good friendships and feeling hurt by other boys in the school.
sentences.zh: 但他们主要谈论的是他们的友谊，试图找到好的友谊，并为学校里其他男孩对他们的伤害感到难过。

sentences.en: At first, she was surprised.
sentences.zh: 起初，她感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: When I started to hear boys, it was at first wondering why they weren't sounding like the boys I thought they were going to sound like.
sentences.zh: 当我开始听到男孩们说话时，起初我很纳闷为什么他们听起来不像我想象的那样。

sentences.en: And so essentially, it was why didn't they sound like the stereotypes that I had of them, whether it was boys or as working class boys or as boys of color, etc.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上就是，为什么他们听起来不像我对他们的固有刻板印象，无论是作为男孩、工人阶级男孩还是有色人种男孩等等。

sentences.en: I was thinking they were talking a lot about, you know, friendships.
sentences.zh: 我以为他们会谈论很多关于，你知道的，友谊的事情。

sentences.en: They sounded like, quote unquote, in my head in the late 80s, like girls.
sentences.zh: 在80年代末的我脑海里，他们听起来，引用的说，就像女孩一样。

sentences.en: She wanted to know what was wrong with the boys, not what was wrong with the stereotype.
sentences.zh: 她想知道的是男孩们出了什么问题，而不是刻板印象出了什么问题。

sentences.en: That's how stereotypes work.
sentences.zh: 这就是刻板印象的作用方式。

sentences.en: We know that they're not true for ourselves, but we somehow think they're true for other people.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这些刻板印象对我们自己不适用，但我们不知为何认为它们适用于其他人。

sentences.en: As Niobe studied the issue, she discovered that men in other cultures and American men in other times had no problem developing close, intimate friendships well into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 正如尼奥比研究所研究的那样，她发现其他文化中的男性以及其他时期的美国男性在成年后建立亲密的友谊并没有任何问题。

sentences.en: And the men she knew, at least at one point in their lives, had no problem being deeply and openly emotional.
sentences.zh: 而且她认识的男性，至少在他们人生的某个阶段，在表现出深刻而公开的情感方面也没有任何问题。

sentences.en: I actually had very, very clear memories of my brothers having similar kinds of friendships.
sentences.zh: 我实际上有非常非常清晰的记忆，我的兄弟们也有过类似类型的友谊。

sentences.en: Niobe remembers a time when she was sitting upstairs in her parents' house, and she could hear her younger brother and his friends outside.
sentences.zh: 尼奥比记得有一次她坐在父母家的楼上，能听到她弟弟和他的朋友们在外面。

sentences.en: He was out in the backyard talking with his basketball teammates.
sentences.zh: 他在后院和他的篮球队队友聊天。

sentences.en: One of the guys had said something mean to one of the other guys in the group.
sentences.zh: 其中一个家伙对群里的另一个家伙说了刻薄的话。

sentences.en: And the four of them were processing their feelings around this mean behavior by one of the boys towards the other boys.
sentences.zh: 他们四个人正在梳理他们对其中一个男孩对另一个男孩这种刻薄行为的感受。

sentences.en: And these were four tough-looking basketball players, athletic, cool kids in the high school.
sentences.zh: 这些都是四个看起来很硬朗的篮球运动员，身材健美，是高中里很酷的孩子。

sentences.en: And they were all sitting there for about an hour processing these feelings with each other.
sentences.zh: 他们都在那里坐了一个小时，互相梳理着这些情绪。

sentences.en: Then she remembered how her other brother had a falling out with his best friend when he was a preteen.
sentences.zh: 然后她想起她的另一个兄弟在青春期前夕与他最好的朋友闹翻了。

sentences.en: I remember the enormous sadness of my brother around that sort of immediate, sort of dramatic departure of a friendship.
sentences.zh: 我记得我的兄弟面对那种友谊的突然、戏剧性的破裂时感到的巨大悲伤。

sentences.en: All this started to change how Niobe listened.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切开始改变尼奥比倾听的方式。

sentences.en: I realized it was all around me, that lots of boys, my brothers, my friends, my all sorts of boys and young men,
sentences.zh: 我意识到这就在我身边，许多男孩、我的兄弟们、我的朋友们、各种各样的男孩和年轻男性，

sentences.en: were talking about this desire or having these close friendships or desiring it.
sentences.zh: 都在谈论这种渴望，或者拥有这些亲密的友谊，或者对此充满渴望。

sentences.en: Niobe took these observations with her as she went on to get a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 尼奥比带着这些观察结果继续去攻读博士学位。

sentences.en: She eventually became a developmental psychologist at NYU.
sentences.zh: 她最终成为了纽约大学的发展心理学家。

sentences.en: She's interviewed hundreds of boys since then, often circling back to the same kids year after year.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，她采访了数百名男孩，常常年复一年地回访相同的孩子。

sentences.en: The overwhelming majority have told her things like this, which she heard from a 15-year-old named Justin.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人都对她说过这样的话，这是她从一个名叫贾斯廷的15岁男孩那里听到的。

sentences.en: We had teenage actors read the quotes.
sentences.zh: 我们请了少年演员来朗读这些引言。

sentences.en: My best friend and I love each other.
sentences.zh: 我和我最好的朋友彼此相爱。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: You have this thing that is so deep, it's within you.
sentences.zh: 你有这样一种东西，它是如此深厚，它就在你的内心深处。

sentences.en: You can't explain it.
sentences.zh: 你无法解释它。

sentences.en: It's just the thing that, you know, that that person is that person.
sentences.zh: 它只是一种你知道的那个人就是那个人的感觉。

sentences.en: And that's all that should be important in our friendship.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的友谊中唯一应该重要的全部。

sentences.en: I guess in life sometimes, two people can really, really understand each other and really have a trust, respect and love for each other.
sentences.zh: 我想生活中有时两个人真的能真正理解彼此，并且真正对彼此产生信任、尊重和爱。

sentences.en: It just happens.
sentences.zh: 它自然而然地发生了。

sentences.en: It's like human nature.
sentences.zh: 这就像是人性。

sentences.en: She heard this about the importance of close friends from a 16-year-old.
sentences.zh: 她从一个16岁男孩那里听到了关于密友重要性的这番话。

sentences.en: I mean, if you just have your mother and your parents to talk to,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你只有你的母亲和父母可以倾诉，

sentences.en: then you're just going to have all these ideas bottled up and you're just going to go wacko because you can't express yourself.
sentences.zh: 那么你就会把所有这些想法都憋在心里，然后你就会发疯，因为你无法表达自己。

sentences.en: But as the boys got older, something happened.
sentences.zh: 但随着男孩们长大，事情发生了变化。

sentences.en: It became harder for them to express tenderness and vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 他们变得更难表达温柔和脆弱了。

sentences.en: Boys who had talked about how they loved their best friend or would go wacko without them began to sound more like a stereotype of teenage boys,
sentences.zh: 那些曾谈论过他们如何爱自己最好朋友或者没有对方就会发疯的男孩，开始听起来更像是对十几岁男孩的刻板印象，

sentences.en: the ones who didn't want to have anything to do with touchy-feely stuff.
sentences.zh: 即那些不想和感性、黏糊糊的事情有任何瓜葛的人。

sentences.en: Some of the boys go into sort of, I don't care, it doesn't matter, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 有些男孩会表现得好像，我不在乎，这无所谓，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But they say, I don't care so many times that you sense exactly that they do very much care.
sentences.zh: 但他们说“我不在乎”的次数如此之多，以至于你分明能感觉到他们其实非常在乎。

sentences.en: Some of the older boys did talk to Niobe about the sadness they felt at disappearing friendships.
sentences.zh: 一些年龄较大的男孩确实向尼奥比谈到了他们对友谊消逝所感受到的悲伤。

sentences.en: A high school senior described how his friendships have changed since freshman year.
sentences.zh: 一名高中高年级学生描述了他的友谊自高一以来是如何改变的。

sentences.en: My friendship with my best friend is fading, but I'm saying it's still there.
sentences.zh: 我和我最好朋友的友谊正在褪色，但我可以说它仍然存在。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's still there because we still do stuff together, but only once in a while.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，它仍然存在，因为我们仍然一起做事，但只是偶尔。

sentences.en: It's sad because he lives only one block away from me and I get to do stuff with him less than I get to do stuff for people who are way further.
sentences.zh: 这很让人难过，因为他只住在我家隔壁一个街区，而我和他一起做事的频率甚至比我和那些住得很远的人一起做事的频率还要低。

sentences.en: So, I'm like, it's like a DJ used his crossfader and started fading it slowly and slowly.
sentences.zh: 所以，我就觉得，这就像一个DJ使用了交叉推子，开始慢慢地、慢慢地把它调淡。

sentences.en: And now I'm like halfway through the crossfade.
sentences.zh: 而现在我感觉自己正处于交叉淡化的中间阶段。

sentences.en: This is the language of boys.
sentences.zh: 这就是男孩们的语言。

sentences.en: I mean, this is just, you know, remarkably beautiful language about talking about how they're feeling and what's happening in the relational world around them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是，你知道的，非常美丽的语言，用来谈论他们的感受以及他们周围关系世界中正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So, the idea is that boys aren't just being emotional.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个观点是，男孩们不仅仅是在情绪化。

sentences.en: They're actually reading the world in a beautiful, you know, articulate way, which is exactly how they're stereotyped not to be able to do.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上在以一种美丽的、你知道的、清晰的方式解读这个世界，而这恰恰是刻板印象中认为他们做不到的。

sentences.en: The stereotype that boys are less emotional than girls doesn't hold up when Niobe interviews boys.
sentences.zh: 当尼奥比采访男孩时，男孩比女孩更缺乏情感的刻板印象根本站不住脚。

sentences.en: These are human beings with unbelievable emotional and social capacity.
sentences.zh: 这些是具有难以置信的情感和社会能力的人类。

sentences.en: And we as a culture just completely try to zip it out of them.
sentences.zh: 而我们作为一种文化，却极力试图将这些从他们身上抹杀掉。

sentences.en: And we ignore it.
sentences.zh: 我们对此视而不见。

sentences.en: Niobe has an explanation for why boys have trouble maintaining close bonds with one another.
sentences.zh: 对于为什么男孩很难与彼此保持密切的联系，尼奥比给出了一个解释。

sentences.en: The reason for that struggle really is quite simple, which is that it's American masculinity and masculine norms and masculine expectations
sentences.zh: 造成这种挣扎的原因其实很简单，那就是美国的男子气概、男性规范和男性的期望，

sentences.en: that make, you know, close friendships into a girly gay thing rather than simply a human thing.
sentences.zh: 让亲密的友谊变成了娘娘腔、同性恋的事情，而不是单纯的人类的的事情。

sentences.en: So, as boys grow older and enter manhood, they begin to be overwhelmed with this expectation that somehow they have to be, you know, on their own.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着男孩长大并进入成年，他们开始被这样一种期望所淹没：不知何故，他们必须，你知道的，靠自己。

sentences.en: They can't depend on others.
sentences.zh: 他们不能依赖他人。

sentences.en: They have to be fully independent.
sentences.zh: 他们必须完全独立。

sentences.en: That somehow the desire for intimacy with other boys is problematic in a culture that's very hyper-masculine.
sentences.zh: 在一种极度崇尚男子气概的文化中，对与其他男孩建立亲密关系的渴望不知何故成了有问题的事情。

sentences.en: This hyper-masculinity, boys pick it up quickly and unconsciously.

sentences.en: Even parents buy into the idea that there's something to be concerned about if their teenage boys appear sensitive and vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 甚至连父母也认同这样一种观念：如果他们十几岁的儿子表现得敏感脆弱，那就有什么地方是令人担忧的。

sentences.en: I think parents sometimes even get anxious when their boys sound like this.
sentences.zh: 我认为父母有时甚至会在他们的儿子听起来像这样时感到焦虑。

sentences.en: So, even when, you know, you hear parents talking about their kids being very sensitive,
sentences.zh: 所以，甚至当你知道父母谈论他们的孩子非常敏感时，

sentences.en: it's oftentimes with their sons, there's oftentimes an embarrassment about it.
sentences.zh: 很多时候对于他们的儿子来说，这种敏感往往伴随着一种尴尬。

sentences.en: And parents certainly aren't, you know, judging their sons in the same ways.
sentences.zh: 而且父母当然不会以同样的方式去评判他们的儿子。

sentences.en: But parents are part of the culture just like everybody else.
sentences.zh: 但父母和其他人一样，也是这种文化的一部分。

sentences.en: Niobe has had parents come to her and say,
sentences.zh: 尼奥比曾遇到过父母来找她并说，

sentences.en: You know, I think my son is gay.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得我儿子是同性恋。

sentences.en: And I'll say, oh, okay, so, you know, what makes you think that?
sentences.zh: 然后我会说，哦，好吧，所以，你知道，是什么让你这么觉得的？

sentences.en: And they'll say, well, you know, he's very sensitive.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会说，嗯，你知道的，他非常敏感。

sentences.en: And, you know, that to me is as depressing as the comment about it might be nice to be a girl.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，对我来说，这和那种“当个女孩也许挺好”的评论一样令人沮丧。

sentences.en: Because then, you know, you wouldn't have to be emotionless.
sentences.zh: 因为那样的话，你知道的，你就不用表现得毫无感情了。

sentences.en: Because the idea is that, first of all, of course, being gay is as joyous, as wonderful as being straight.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的观点首先是，当然，同性恋和异性恋一样充满快乐、一样美好。

sentences.en: But, you know, the fact that they're equating sexuality with being sensitive,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，他们把性取向与敏感等同起来，这一事实……

sentences.en: I mean, it has nothing to do with sexuality.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这跟性取向毫无关系。

sentences.en: Niobe doesn't ask the boys she interviews about their sexual orientation.
sentences.zh: 尼奥比不会向她采访的男孩询问他们的性取向。

sentences.en: Some of them might, indeed, be gay.
sentences.zh: 他们当中确实有些人可能是同性恋。

sentences.en: But she thinks that boys of all sexual orientations find themselves in straight jackets
sentences.zh: 但她认为，各种性取向的男孩都身处无形的束缚之中，

sentences.zh: 这种束缚告诉他们，如果表现得过度情绪化，就是有什么不对劲。

sentences.en: To put this another way, the problem of hypermasculinity doesn't just affect straight boys
sentences.zh: 换句话说，过度男子气概的问题不仅仅影响那些担心被视为同性恋的异性恋男孩。

sentences.en: who are worried about appearing gay.

sentences.en: The model of the tough guy who doesn't need others, who can move through the world without being bruised by it.
sentences.zh: 这种“不需要他人、能毫发无损地闯荡世界”的硬汉模式，

sentences.en: This model affects all boys.
sentences.zh: 这种模式影响着所有的男孩。

sentences.en: When boys lose their close friendships, there's more at stake than sleepovers
sentences.zh: 当男孩们失去亲密的友谊时，面临的风险不仅仅是留宿派对，

sentences.en: and having someone to sit next to on the way to school.
sentences.zh: 以及在上学路上能有个坐在旁边的人。

sentences.en: Niobe thinks there are consequences for mental health.
sentences.zh: 尼奥比认为这对心理健康有负面影响。

sentences.en: I just don't think it's just coincidental that at the very time you hear their language,

sentences.zh: 他们言语中的爱意、他们言语中的情感共鸣开始减少，

sentences.zh: 而愤怒、挫败感、“我不在乎”的语气开始出现在他们的故事中时，

sentences.zh: 恰恰也是自杀率上升的时候。

sentences.en: There is no hard evidence that the decline of friendships among adolescent boys is responsible for suicide.
sentences.zh: 没有确凿的证据表明，青春期男孩之间友谊的减少是导致自杀的原因。

sentences.en: But Niobe is worried by a correlation.
sentences.zh: 但尼奥比对这种相关性感到担忧。

sentences.en: As boys' friendships start to weaken, their diary entries start to reveal mental health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 随着男孩们的友谊开始减弱，他们的日记内容也开始暴露出心理健康问题。

sentences.en: Niobe's concern led her to team up with another professor and a middle school teacher.
sentences.zh: 尼奥比的担忧促使她与另一位教授和一名中学老师组成了团队。

sentences.en: The idea was to help boys connect more deeply with people they cared about.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是为了帮助男孩们与他们关心的人建立更深层次的联系。

sentences.en: How?

sentences.en: Asking them to conduct in-depth interviews with their loved ones.
sentences.zh: 要求他们与自己爱的人进行深入的访谈。

sentences.en: They started the program at an all-boys school and have since expanded it to other schools.
sentences.zh: 他们在一所全男校启动了这个项目，此后已将其扩展到其他学校。

sentences.en: At the top of the show, we heard from two 12-year-olds at one school.
sentences.zh: 在节目刚开始时，我们听取了一所学校里两名12岁男孩的看法。

sentences.en: My producer, Raina Cohen, talked to their classmates.
sentences.zh: 我的制作人雷娜·科恩采访了他们的同班同学。

sentences.en: So, as you get older, it kind of seems like the girls drift closer to the girls and the boys drift closer to the boys
sentences.zh: 所以，随着你年龄的增长，感觉好像女孩更倾向于跟女孩玩，男孩更倾向于跟男孩玩，

sentences.en: because you're going through something that's very similar as the other boys in your grade
sentences.zh: 因为你正在经历和你年级里的其他男孩非常相似的事情，

sentences.en: and the girls are going through something very similar as the girls in their grade.
sentences.zh: 而女孩们正在经历的事情也和她们年级里的女孩非常相似。

sentences.en: So, you kind of group up with someone you have someone in common with.
sentences.zh: 所以，你会倾向于和你有共同点的人聚在一起。

sentences.en: So, friendships, as we get older and we hit puberty, friendships, especially with the other opposite gender,
sentences.zh: 因此，随着我们年龄增长并步入青春期，友谊，尤其是与异性之间的友谊，

sentences.zh: 可能会在某种程度上发生改变。

sentences.zh: 对我来说，这有点吓人，因为我还没真正准备好面对这些。

sentences.en: But, in some cases, like, boys can just be friends with boys and not talk about, like, emotional things.

sentences.en: But, if you're closer friends with that boy, then I think you feel more comfortable talking to them about, like,
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你和那个男孩是更亲密的朋友，那么我想你会更愿意跟他谈论，比如，

sentences.en: what's going on, like, emotionally with you than you would be with one of your not-as-close friends.
sentences.zh: 你情感上发生了什么，而这在那些没那么亲密的朋友面前你可能做不到。

sentences.en: So, I think it's not true that boys don't talk to their friends about personal things.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为“男孩不和朋友谈论个人私事”是不符合事实的。

sentences.en: It's actually easier to talk about personal things with your friends than your parents
sentences.zh: 实际上，跟朋友谈论个人私事比跟父母谈要容易，

sentences.en: because they fully or mostly understand what you're going through
sentences.zh: 因为他们完全或大部分能理解你正在经历什么，

sentences.en: because they're probably going through something similar like that, too.
sentences.zh: 因为他们可能也正在经历类似的事情。

sentences.en: But you wouldn't know that based on the way that boys are portrayed in TV shows and movies.

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为男孩如果想的话是可以表现出情感的，但我觉得他们不会这么做。

sentences.zh: 唯一可以接受的情感表达方式是在恋爱关系中。

sentences.zh: 而且你本该让这些恋爱关系榨干你曾经倾注在友谊中的所有精力。

sentences.zh: 当你交了女朋友时，比如，你必须花很多时间陪她。

sentences.zh: 或者如果你交了男朋友，你必须花很多时间陪他。

sentences.zh: 所以，比如，你花在他们身上的时间会比花在你最好的朋友身上的时间还多。

sentences.en: And then they might get jealous and react.

sentences.en: Of course, this is exactly the kind of thinking that, in 30 or 40 years, leaves middle-aged men bereft of social connection when their marriages fall apart or a spouse dies.
sentences.zh: 当然，正是这种思维方式，在30或40年后，当婚姻破裂或配偶去世时，会让中年男士陷入缺乏社交联系的孤立境地。

sentences.zh: 我们在纽约采访的男孩们已经在吸取这样的教训：社会认为男性之间只有某些特定类型的友谊是可以接受的。

sentences.en: One is the bromance.

sentences.zh: “兄弟情”并不是男人已经超越恐同症的证据。

sentences.en: They're a way for men to dabble in emotional connection while telegraphing to the world that they're absolutely not, not even a little bit, gay.
sentences.zh: 它们只是男人涉足情感连接的一种方式，同时向世界发出电报般的信号：他们绝对不是，哪怕一点点也不是同性恋。

sentences.en: Niobe says some big changes need to happen for emotional 12-year-old boys to grow into emotional 42-year-olds.
sentences.zh: 尼奥比说，12岁的情感丰富男孩要成长为42岁的情感成熟男性，必须发生一些重大的改变。

sentences.en: How do we as a culture change the culture to normalize,
sentences.zh: 我们作为一种文化，该如何改变这种文化，使其正常化，

sentences.en: to humanize this fundamental human need and capacity of reading the human world and engaging with it and having quality relationships?
sentences.zh: 如何将这种解读人类世界、与世界互动并建立高质量关系的基本人类需求和能力人性化？

sentences.en: We can change it because we already know that through gay marriage.
sentences.zh: 我们可以改变它，因为我们已经通过同性婚姻看到了这一点。

sentences.en: We now accept gay marriage as a culture.
sentences.zh: 作为一种文化，我们现在已经接受了同性婚姻。

sentences.en: We can change anything we want to change.
sentences.zh: 任何我们想改变的，我们都可以改变。

sentences.en: Men's fear of appearing gay or feminine isn't the only reason many of us end up lonely.
sentences.zh: 男人对显得像同性恋或女性化的恐惧，并不是我们许多人最终感到孤独的唯一原因。

sentences.en: Both men and women are plagued by a bias that pushes us towards isolation rather than connection.
sentences.zh: 男人和女人都受到一种偏见的困扰，这种偏见把我们推向孤立，而不是连接。

sentences.en: Nick Epley regularly rides the Chicago metro system.
sentences.zh: 尼克·埃普利经常乘坐芝加哥地铁系统。

sentences.en: He was on the train one day when he noticed something puzzling.
sentences.zh: 有一天他在火车上注意到了一件令人困惑的事情。

sentences.en: We happen to be one of the most social species on the planet who seems to get a lot of happiness and satisfaction from our connections with others.
sentences.zh: 我们恰好是地球上最具社交性的物种之一，似乎能从与他人的联系中获得大量的快乐和满足感。

sentences.en: And yet, every morning on the train and over and over again in public spaces where I'd be out and about,
sentences.zh: 然而，每天早晨在火车上，以及在我外出时的公共场所里一次又一次地，

sentences.en: I would see people standing cheek to jowl next to each other or sitting cheek to jowl next to each other and ignoring each other.
sentences.zh: 我会看到人们肩并肩地站着，或者肩并肩地坐着，却彼此忽视。

sentences.en: Nick is a behavioral science professor at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business.
sentences.zh: 尼克是芝加哥大学布斯商学院的行为科学教授。

sentences.en: He started thinking about this odd behavior.
sentences.zh: 他开始思考这种奇怪的行为。

sentences.en: Why do we ignore one another?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么会忽视彼此？

sentences.en: One possibility is that strangers, in fact, are unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 一种可能性是，陌生人事实上并不讨人喜欢。

sentences.en: We don't know them.
sentences.zh: 我们不认识他们。

sentences.en: And striking up a conversation would be less pleasant than sitting there in solitude.
sentences.zh: 主动挑起对话会比一个人静静坐着更让人不快。

sentences.en: So people are maximizing their well-being by sitting on the train or maybe in a cab or on a bus or in a waiting room and ignoring each other.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们在火车上、或者在出租车里、公交车上或候诊室里通过忽视彼此来最大化他们的幸福感。

sentences.en: That's possible.
sentences.zh: 这有可能。

sentences.en: The other possibility is that we actually underestimate the benefits that come from social engagement.
sentences.zh: 另一种可能性是，我们实际上低估了社交互动带来的好处。

sentences.en: That we think we'd be happier sitting in solitude.
sentences.zh: 我们以为自己一个人孤坐会更快乐。

sentences.en: And, in fact, we're just wrong about that.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，我们的这种想法完全是错的。

sentences.en: Nick and his co-author, Juliana Schroeder, decided to figure out what was going on.
sentences.zh: 尼克和他的合著者朱莉安娜·施罗德决定弄清楚到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: They ran an experiment that involved commuters.
sentences.zh: 他们做了一个涉及通勤者的实验。

sentences.en: Volunteers were assigned to one of three conditions.
sentences.zh: 志愿者被分配到三种情况中的一种。

sentences.en: Engage with the people around them, sit in solitude, or act as they normally would on their commute.
sentences.zh: 与周围的人互动，独自静坐，或者像平时通勤那样行事。

sentences.en: People predicted that they would be the least happy if they had to engage with other people on the train.
sentences.zh: 人们预测，如果必须在火车上与其他人互动，他们会感到最不快乐。

sentences.en: They were sure that what would make them happy was to be simply left alone.
sentences.zh: 他们确信能让自己快乐的就是被独自留着别打扰。

sentences.en: But that's not what the study found.
sentences.zh: 但研究结果并非如此。

sentences.en: People reported being happier, less sad, and having a more pleasant commute when they connected with the person sitting next to them
sentences.zh: 与随机分配到被要求独自静坐的情况相比，

sentences.en: than when we randomly assigned them to a condition where they were asked to sit in solitude.
sentences.zh: 当人们与坐在旁边的人建立联系时，他们报告说自己更快乐、不那么悲伤，并且拥有更愉快的通勤体验。

sentences.en: People's perception that their fellow commuters wanted to be left alone didn't match reality.
sentences.zh: 人们认为同车通勤者希望被独自留下的看法与现实不符。

sentences.en: What was happening was that volunteers thought that others were less interested in talking to them than they actually were.
sentences.zh: 实际情况是，志愿者们以为别人对跟他们说话的兴趣，其实比别人真正的兴趣要低。

sentences.en: In one study, volunteers were asked,
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，志愿者被问及：

sentences.en: What percentage of people on the train would be interested in talking to you,
sentences.zh: 火车上有百分之多少的人会对跟你说话感兴趣，

sentences.en: or would be willing to talk to you if you tried?
sentences.zh: 或者如果你尝试的话，他们会愿意跟你说话？

sentences.en: They estimated fewer than 50% of people would.
sentences.zh: 他们估计这一比例不到50%。

sentences.en: As far as we can tell, the actual percentage of people who would be willing to talk to you is much closer to 100%.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，愿意跟你说话的人的实际比例远接近100%。

sentences.en: This distorted belief keeps us, and the strangers around us, from connecting with one another,
sentences.zh: 这种扭曲的信念阻碍了我们以及我们身边的陌生人去建立联系，

sentences.en: opening a conversation, making small talk.
sentences.zh: 阻碍了我们开启对话、进行闲聊。

sentences.en: Hey, I like those pants.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我喜欢那条裤子。

sentences.en: Those are good-looking shoes.
sentences.zh: 这鞋子真好看。

sentences.en: What do you think of the weather today?
sentences.zh: 你觉得今天的天气怎么样？

sentences.en: How long have you been riding this train?
sentences.zh: 你坐这趟车多久了？

sentences.en: Nick says there are two steps to having a pleasant conversation,
sentences.zh: 尼克说，进行一次愉快的对话有两个步骤：

sentences.en: getting it started, and keeping it going.
sentences.zh: 把对话开启，并让对话持续下去。

sentences.en: And what we find in our data is that the barrier seems to be in the first of those things.
sentences.zh: 而我们在数据中发现的是，障碍似乎出在第一步上。

sentences.en: It's not that people anticipate that having a conversation, once it gets going, will be unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 人们并不是预料到一旦聊起来过程会很不愉快。

sentences.en: They think that'll be okay.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得那倒还行。

sentences.en: Instead, the barrier seems to come earlier.
sentences.zh: 相反，障碍似乎出现得更早。

sentences.en: There's anxiety about actually starting the conversation, engaging in the conversation.
sentences.zh: 人们对于真正开启对话、融入对话会感到焦虑。

sentences.en: And that's what seems to lead people to predict that it's going to be unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 正是这种焦虑导致人们预测接下来的交流会很不愉快。

sentences.en: Nick has an analogy.
sentences.zh: 尼克有一个比喻。

sentences.en: It's like climbing up a steep hill.
sentences.zh: 这就像是爬上一座陡峭的山坡。

sentences.en: You've got to get over that initial speed bump at the top, and then after that, it seems to go pretty smoothly.
sentences.zh: 你必须先克服顶峰最初那个减速带，之后一切似乎就会顺畅多了。

sentences.en: But if you don't get over that first initial bump, you'll never get started.
sentences.zh: 但如果你无法跨过最初的那道坎，你就永远无法开始。

sentences.en: Of course, not everyone has the same freedom to chat with strangers in the way Nick suggests.
sentences.zh: 当然，并非所有人都能像尼克建议的那样，拥有同等自由去与陌生人闲聊。

sentences.en: Our gender, race, appearance, and many other factors affect how people view us.
sentences.zh: 我们的性别、种族、外表以及许多其他因素都会影响人们对我们的看法。

sentences.en: In some contexts, it can be dangerous to start a conversation with a stranger.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，跟陌生人搭话可能会有危险。

sentences.en: But what's clear from many of the messages we receive from Hidden Brain listeners is that the desire for connection is deep, and in many cases, unfulfilled.
sentences.zh: 但从我们收到的大量《Hidden Brain》听众留言中可以清楚看出，人们对建立联系的渴望是极其深切的，而在许多情况下，这种渴望并未得到满足。

sentences.en: Loneliness and social isolation has become more and more part of my daily life.
sentences.zh: 孤独感和社会孤立越来越多地融入我的日常生活。

sentences.en: It's harder to find situations that I enjoy being in.
sentences.zh: 要找到让我乐在其中的场合变得更难了。

sentences.en: I have two or three friends that I've known since we were all teenagers.
sentences.zh: 我有两三个从青少年时期就认识的朋友。

sentences.en: And other than that, if my wife weren't around, I would be hard-pressed to have close friends other than those from a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，如果我妻子不在身边，除了那些老朋友外，我很难再交到什么亲密朋友。

sentences.en: We have perhaps more of a reason to turn to people and to wean on those friendships and those relationships to give us strength,
sentences.zh: 我们或许更有理由向他人求助，依靠这些友谊和关系来给我们力量，

sentences.en: but they're often not there in the way that they are for women or they were, you know, when we were hanging out with our friends in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 但它们往往不像对女性那样存在，或者不像我们二十多岁时和朋友厮混时那样。

sentences.en: Think how much better life could be if we could just admit these things to someone we care about, not just to a voicemail inbox.
sentences.zh: 试想一下，如果我们能向真正在乎的人坦白这些事情，而不只是对着语音信箱倾诉，生活会变得多么美好。

sentences.en: If we could be okay with being vulnerable, with being dependent on someone who's not a spouse.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能坦然接受脆弱，坦然依赖配偶以外的人。

sentences.en: If we didn't look suspiciously at older men who are friendly or shame boys who talk about their love for their friends.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不再用怀疑的眼光看待友善的老年男性，也不再羞辱那些表达对朋友爱意的男孩。

sentences.en: If we expected friendships to endure, even as our lives change, so they don't have to fade to silence.
sentences.zh: 如果我们期望友谊能够长存，哪怕生活发生变化，也不至于让友谊归于沉寂。

sentences.zh: 本期节目由雷娜·科恩制作，塔拉·博伊尔编辑。

sentences.zh: 特别感谢埃米尔和芬恩·博比安，他们朗读了节目中你听到的引言。

sentences.en: Our unsung hero this week is Gina Voskov.
sentences.zh: 我们本周的幕后英雄吉娜·沃斯科夫。

sentences.en: She's a teacher at the United Nations International School.
sentences.zh: 她是联合国国际学校的一名老师。

sentences.en: She helped us arrange interviews with a group of 7th and 8th grade boys.
sentences.zh: 她帮我们安排了与一群七、八年级男生采访的事宜。

sentences.en: She kindly managed a long string of emails as she coordinated between our producer, the students, and their parents.
sentences.zh: 她亲切地处理了大量电子邮件，在我们的制作人、学生和家长之间进行协调。

sentences.en: Thank you, Gina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，吉娜。

sentences.en: If you like this show, here's an important thing you can do for us, and an important thing you can do for yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这个节目，这里有一件你能为我们做的事，也是一件你能为自己做的事。

sentences.en: Tell one friend about our show, and consider striking up a conversation with a stranger this week.
sentences.zh: 把我们的节目推荐给一位朋友，并考虑在本周试着跟一个陌生人搭话。

sentences.en: If you can't think of anything else to say, ask them,
sentences.zh: 如果你想不出别的话说，就问他们：

sentences.en: Hey, do you listen to Hidden Brain?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你听过《Hidden Brain》吗？

sentences.en: Tell us what happens next on Facebook or Twitter.
sentences.zh: 在脸书或推特上告诉我们接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆，这里是NPR。
